answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network imposes a quadratic stake-burning mechanism. When an identity registers during each epoch pulse, it must burn cryptographic tokens proportional to the square of active network nodes. A genuine participant easily covers this baseline, but a Sybil attacker attempting to flood the graph sees marginal costs scale superlinearly as O(k^2). If an attacker’s resources hit a nadir, rapid stake evaporation extinguishes their replicas like a blazing comet, ensuring economic friction dominates malicious identity replication.
